title: Errors: what is failing, and which fault

options.content:
Two questions. Different signals answer them, on purpose, per ADR-0503.

**How much** is `errors_total{service, kind}`. It is a bounded metric with five `kind` values, and it is the only thing here that alerts. **Which fault** is `error.fingerprint`. It is structured log metadata and a span attribute, and it is *never* a metric or stream label. So it is queried from the log store below, and not aggregated in Prometheus. This follows the cardinality rules of ADR-0500.

There is no persistent fingerprint store on this floor. So the check for a new fault compares two windows, and is not a lookup. It catches a new fault within the window. It misses a fault that appeared and stopped inside the window. That guarantee is narrower than a tracker's, and not the same.

panels.title: Error rate by kind
panels.description: The bounded metric. A shift between kinds often explains the fault. If dependency rises while internal is flat, something else fails, and not this service.

panels.title: Error rate by service
panels.description: The variable above does not filter this panel, on purpose. This panel shows whether one service fails or the whole platform does.

panels.title: Faults in the last hour, by fingerprint
panels.description: Grouped by the computed fingerprint, so one row is one fault, however many times it happened. The count is the number of occurrences. Open a row to reach the trace.

panels.title: Fingerprints seen this hour and not the hour before
panels.description: The new-fault check, as a query and not as state, per ADR-0503. A row here is a fault whose first occurrence is inside this window. It is a set difference over two windows. So a fault that appeared and stopped within the previous hour does not show. That is the accepted gap, not a bug.

targets.expr: sum by (fingerprint) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service"} | json | fingerprint != "" [1h])) unless sum by (fingerprint) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service"} | json | fingerprint != "" [1h] offset 1h))

panels.title: Recent error logs
panels.description: The raw stream behind the tables. `fingerprint` is structured metadata here, never a stream label. A filter on it is a line filter, so these queries parse and do not select.
